New approaches to the Erdős Distinct Subset Sums Problem

**Abstract**

We present a new method of reproving the best known lower bound of the Erdős distinct subset sums problem. Although our lower bound is asymptotically the same as in [4], it is slightly better for the case when _n_ is odd. Besides, we also provide a new lower bound on the second largest element _a_<sub>_n_-1</sub>.

## 1 Introduction

Let

\(A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n\}\)

be a set of positive integers whose subset sums are all distinct. The Erdős distinct subset sums problem asks how small the largest element _a<sub>n</sub>_ can be. In particular, Erdős asked whether there exists an absolute constant _c\>_0 such that \(a_n\ge c2^n\) and offered 500$ for proving or disproving [6], which was claimed to be disproved by GPT-6 Astra in 2026. The classical variance method gives a lower bound of order \(2^n/\sqrt{n}\), with subsequent improvements by Elkies [5], Bae [2], and Aliev [1]. Dubroff, Fox, and Xu obtained the asymptotic lower bound

\(a_n\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n}}\)

and provided two short proofs of this estimate [4]. In the opposite direction, before GPT-6 Astra, the best known upper bound was by Bohman, who constructed sets with

\(a_n<0.220022^n\)

for all sufficiently large _n_ [3].

## 2 Main results

Let

\(A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n\}\)

be a set of positive integers with distinct subset sums, and put

\(T=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}a_j.\)

Write the subset sums of _a_<sub>1</sub>_,...,a_<sub>_n_-1</sub> in increasing order:<tbc>

\(0=t_1<t_2<\cdots<t_{2^{n-1}}=T.\)

<tbc>**Theorem 1.** If \(a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n\) are positive integers with distinct subset sums, then

\(a_n\ge 2\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor}.\)

In our proof, we combine ideas from \[4\] with the following observations. If _a<sub>n</sub>_ is \(\Omega(2^n)\), then the theorem is proven, i.e., we may assume that _a<sub>n</sub>=o_(2_<sup>n</sup>_).

**Lemma 1.** If \(i+a_n\le 2^{n-1}\), then<tbc>

\(t_{i+a_n}-t_i\ge 2a_n.\)

<tbc>_Proof._ Consider the _a<sub>n</sub>_+1 integers<tbc>

\(t_i,t_{i+1},\dots,t_{i+a_n}.\)

<tbc>By the pigeonhole principle, two of them, say _t<sub>k</sub>_ and \(t_\ell\), with \(k<\ell\), are congruent modulo _a<sub>n</sub>_. Hence<tbc>

\(t_\ell-t_k=ma_n\)

<tbc>for some positive integer _m_.

If _m_=1, then<tbc>

\(t_\ell=t_k+a_n.\)

<tbc>The left-hand side is a subset sum of _a_<sub>1</sub>_,...,a_<sub>_n_-1</sub>, while the right-hand side is a subset sum involving _a<sub>n</sub>_. This contradicts the distinctness of all subset sums. Therefore \(m\ge 2\), and

\(t_{i+a_n}-t_i\ge t_\ell-t_k\ge 2a_n.\)

**Lemma 2.** Define<tbc>

\(\mathcal{F}=\left\{I\subseteq[n-1]:\sum_{j\in I}a_j<\frac{T}{2}\right\}=\left\{t_i:t_i<\frac{T}{2}\right\}.\)

<tbc>Then<tbc>

\(|\mathcal{F}|=2^{n-2}.\)

<tbc>_Proof._ For any \(1\le i\le 2^{n-1}\), _t<sub>i</sub>+t_<sub>2<sup>_n_-1</sup>+1-_i_</sub>=_T_. Since all subset sums are distinct, no subset sum equals _T/_2. So, exactly one member of each pair belongs to F. Therefore,

\(|\mathcal{F}|=2^{n-2}.\)

Now, like in \[4\], identify subsets of \[_n_-1\] with vertices of the (_n_-1)-dimensional Boolean cube. For a family \(\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n-1]}\), let \(\partial\mathcal{F}\) denote its external vertex boundary. Harper’s vertex- isoperimetric inequality implies that if<tbc>

\(|\mathcal{F}|=2^{n-2},\)

then<tbc>

\(|\partial\mathcal{F}|\ge\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}.\)

<tbc>From this, we can conclude that<tbc>

\(\#\left\{t_i:\frac{T}{2}-t_i<a_{n-1}\right\}\ge\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}.\)

<tbc>As _t<sub>i</sub>_-s are symmetric with respect to \(\frac{T}{2}\) and _a<sub>n</sub>\>a_<sub>_n_-1</sub>, we can conclude<tbc>

\(\#\left\{t_i:\left|t_i-\frac{T}{2}\right|<a_n\right\}\ge\#\left\{t_i:\left|t_i-\frac{T}{2}\right|<a_{n-1}\right\}\ge 2\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}.\)

<tbc>**Lemma 3.**<tbc>

\(a_n\ge\#\left\{t_i:\left|t_i-\frac{T}{2}\right|<a_n\right\}.\)

<tbc>_Proof._ Consider the interval

\(J=\left(\frac{T}{2}-a_n,\frac{T}{2}+a_n\right),\)

whose length is 2_a<sub>n</sub>_.

If _J_ contained _a<sub>n</sub>_+1 consecutive subset sums<tbc>

\(t_i,t_{i+1},\dots,t_{i+a_n},\)

<tbc>then

\(t_{i+a_n}-t_i<2a_n,\)

contradicting the first lemma. Therefore _J_ contains at most _a<sub>n</sub>_ subset sums.

Hence, we can conclude from those lemmas that

\(a_n\ge 2\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor},\)

which is exactly the statement of the theorem.

**Asymptotic consequence.**

Using the central-binomial-coefficient estimate<tbc>

\(\genfrac(){pt}{2}{m}{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}=\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^m}{\sqrt{m}},\)

<tbc>the conditional bound in the theorem yields

\(a_n\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n-1}}\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n}}.\)

This is of the same asymptotic order as the established lower bound discussed by Dubroff, Fox, and Xu \[4\]. It is also worth mentioning that this lower bound is better for odd _n_, since if _n_ is odd, then \(2\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}>\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\), as \(2\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n-1}{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}-\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}=C_{\frac{n-1}{2}}\) , where \(C_{\frac{n-1}{2}}\) is the \(\frac{n-1}{2}\) -th Catalan number.

## 3 Some remarks on the second largest element For this subsection, again distinguish the subset sums of all _n_ elements from those of the first _n_-1 elements. Write \(0=t_1j}(t_i-t_j)^2.\) _Proof._ Since _t_1_,...,t_2_n_-1 are all the subset sums of _a_1_,...,a__n_-1, we have \(\sum_{i>j}(t_i-t_j)^2=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{2^{n-1}}(t_i-t_j)^2\)
\(=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{2^{n-1}}(t_i^2+t_j^2-2t_it_j)\)
\(=2^{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}t_i^2-\left(\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}t_i\right)^2.\) Each _ai_ appears in exactly 2_n_-2 subset sums. Hence \(\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}t_i=2^{n-2}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i=2^{n-2}T.\) Moreover, expanding the squares of all subset sums, each \(a_i^2\) appears 2_n_-2 times, while each product _aiaj_, with _i\_n_-3 times. Therefore, \(\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}t_i^2=2^{n-2}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2+2^{n-2}\sum_{1\le i \(=2^{n-3}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2+T^2\right),\) where we used \(T^2=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2+2\sum_{1\le i

Substituting these expressions gives \(\sum_{i>j}(t_i-t_j)^2=2^{n-1}\cdot 2^{n-3}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2+T^2\right)-2^{2n-4}T^2\)
\(=2^{2n-4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2\)
\(=\frac{2^{2(n-1)}}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2.\) From Lemma 1, we have \(t_i-t_j\ge 2a_n\left\lfloor\frac{i-j}{a_n}\right\rfloor.\) Therefore, \(\frac{2^{2(n-1)}}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2\ge 4a_n^2\sum_{i>j}\left\lfloor\frac{i-j}{a_n}\right\rfloor^2\)
\(\ge(1-o(1))4a_n^2\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor 2^{n-1}/a_n\rfloor} k^2a_n(2^{n-1}-ka_n)\)
\(=(1-o(1))4a_n^3\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor 2^{n-1}/a_n\rfloor}\left(2^{n-1}k^2-a_nk^3\right)\)
\(\ge(1-o(1))4a_n^3\left(\frac{2^{n-1}}{3}\frac{2^{3(n-1)}}{a_n^3}-\frac{a_n}{4}\frac{2^{4(n-1)}}{a_n^4}\right)\)
\(=(1-o(1))\frac{2^{4(n-1)}}{3}.\) Hence, \(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2\ge(1-o(1))\frac{2^{2n}}{3}.\) Since \(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i^2\le(n-1)a_{n-1}^2,\) we obtain \((n-1)a_{n-1}^2\ge(1-o(1))\frac{2^{2n}}{3}.\) Consequently, \(a_{n-1}\ge\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n-1}}=\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^{n-1}}{\sqrt{n-1}},\) which is better than the lower bound obtained directly, i.e., \(a_{n-1}\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}-o(1)\right)\frac{2^{n-1}}{\sqrt{n-1}}\).
